records.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the future of society: a multidisciplinary analysis of economic transformation, human behavior, education, and digital governance
records.authors: Asad Ullah; Faisal Rahman; Shaafia Malik; Mahrukh Akhtar; Aliya Pervaiz; Saqib Latif; Shumaira Rahim
records.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has quickly transitioned from a niche technological innovation into a growing and powerful force that is transforming the nature of work, the workplace, education, communication, creative processes, and public decision-making. Its increasing visibility poses significant challenges to the way societies will adapt to the new economic organization, new ways of acting, learning and digital governance. This qualitative research focuses on these intertwined transformations from a multidisciplinary perspective as part of a body of work that tends to explore each of the economic, behavioral, educational, and governance aspects of GenAI separately. The study follows an interpretivist research perspective for a qualitative analysis of the documentary, content analysis of scholarly articles, and thematic synthesis of scholarly documents, policy documents, and authoritative institutional sources to uncover broader patterns in the societal development of GenAI. The analysis reveals six interrelated themes: changing characteristics of knowledge work and economic activity, shifting patterns of human cognition, creativity, communication and agency, restructuring of teaching, learning and assessment, inequalities in access and AI literacy, new concerns over privacy, bias, misinformation, IP and accountability, and the need for adaptive and human-driven digital governance. The results indicate that GenAI should not be seen as an instrument of technological advancement or a guarantee of social turmoil. Instead, its impacts on society are mediated through the ways these technologies are incorporated into pre-existing social systems by institutions, government, teachers, institutions/organisations and individuals. The study builds on interdisciplinary scholarship by linking the economic, behavioral, educational, and governance perspectives in a single qualitative framework. It calls on for more robust governance, human oversight, access, and AI literacy, as well as more ethical institutional practices, to ensure effective and responsible adoption of AI.

records.title: UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES AND THE INTERNET OF THINGS IN AGRICULTURE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF TECHNOLOGICAL DIRECTIONS AND DEVELOPMENT PROSPECTS
records.authors: Volodymyr Panchenko; Heorhii Kuchuk
records.abstract: Relevance. Modern agriculture is undergoing a profound cyber-physical transformation driven by the need to shift from extensive to precision, high-accuracy, and environmentally balanced production methods. The technological foundation of this transition is the integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and wireless Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks, which together form the concept of Agriculture 5.0. Despite the rapid growth of publications on this topic, the accumulated body of research remains fragmented across directions (computer vision, network technologies, robotics, adoption economics), which complicates the formation of a holistic picture of the field and of priority directions for further research. The subject of this study are methods and technologies of applying UAVs and IoT networks to precision-agriculture tasks. The purpose of the article to systematize and classify current scientific research on the use of UAVs and IoT in agriculture, and to determine the leading technological directions, their quantitative proportions, and promising development vectors. The following results were obtained. A total of 198 scientific publications from 2024-2026 were processed and classified into seven thematic classes: crop health and biological threat monitoring, hardware engineering, edge computing and spraying, navigation, swarm intelligence and data collection, phenotyping, biomass and yield forecasting, soil science, water balance and precision irrigation, economics, ecology and socio-cultural perception, and specialized agrotechnical operations. For each class, consolidated tables of applied methods and results, as well as diagrams revealing the internal structure of the direction, were constructed. The dominance of navigation/swarm-control tasks and biological-threat monitoring was identified, along with key technical barriers (limited battery energy density, beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight regulations, and fragmentation of data-exchange standards). Conclusion. The obtained results provide a holistic assessment of the state and structure of the research field on UAV and IoT applications in agriculture and can serve as a basis for shaping further research programs and educational courses in precision agriculture. Future research directions concern improving the energy autonomy of platforms, standardizing data-exchange protocols, and developing edge artificial-intelligence models resilient to complex field conditions.

records.title: Wildfire digital twins: a paradigm shift from monitoring systems to intelligent decision infrastructures
records.authors: Chaowei Yang; Anusha Srirenganathan Malarvizhi; Qunying Huang; Manzhu Yu; Rakshita Chidananda; Mohammad Pourhomayoun; Joe T. Roberts; George W. Chang; Sina Hasheminassab; Grace Llewellyn; Olga Kalashnikova
records.abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent, severe, and complex driven by global warming and climate change, posing escalating threats to ecosystems, infrastructure, public health, and community safety worldwide. Recent advances in Earth observation, artificial intelligence, physics-based modelling, and cyberinfrastructure have accelerated the development of wildfire digital twins (WFDTs), yet existing capabilities remain fragmented across monitoring, fusion, prediction, simulation, and decision support. Unlike prior reviews that primarily address individual aspect of wildfire, this review and vision paper provides an integrated synthesis of WFDTs. We propose a six-layer WFDT architecture, identify six core capabilities spanning situational awareness through adaptive learning, and organise applications across the wildfire lifecycle from prevention and detection to response, smoke management, and post-fire recovery. Building upon these advances, we outline a research roadmap toward autonomous WFDTs through advances in hybrid intelligence, trustworthy AI, uncertainty quantification, decision intelligence, and continual learning. We envision that the defining characteristic of future WFDTs is not increasingly realistic digital representation, but their evolution into a new paradigm that continuously integrates sensing, prediction, uncertainty quantification, optimisation, governance, and human expertise towards a paradigm of intelligent, trustworthy decision infrastructures that continuously support human-centred wildfire decision making.

records.title: Social exclusion in educational settings and the risk of alienation in adolescent development: a narrative review from a mind-body interaction perspective
records.authors: Di Lu; Yumeng Kong; Jinwu Tang
records.abstract: Introduction Social exclusion in educational settings is a salient interpersonal stressor during adolescence. However, ostracism, peer rejection, peer victimization, bullying, loneliness, and social isolation are overlapping but non-equivalent constructs. This narrative review examines how social exclusion in educational settings may contribute to the risk of alienation in adolescent development from a mind-body interaction perspective. Methods A structured, non-exhaustive literature search was conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, and the Web of Science Core Collection for peer-reviewed English-language publications from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2026, supplemented by backward citation tracking. Evidence was organized by construct, population, study design, and biological level. Direct adolescent human findings were distinguished from related adolescent, adult or clinical human, and animal or cellular evidence. Results Direct adolescent studies indicate that peer victimization and interpersonal stress can be associated with heightened peripheral cytokine reactivity, particularly among youths with additional cognitive or developmental vulnerabilities. Developmental neuroscience and neuroimmunology identify plausible endothelial, vagal, glial, synaptic, white-matter, hippocampal, and network pathways through which immune signals could interact with adolescent brain maturation. Nevertheless, the literature does not establish a continuous causal sequence from school exclusion to central neuroinflammation, altered neural plasticity, alienation, or educational impairment. Discussion The evidence supports a conditional, evidence-graded mind-body framework rather than a deterministic pathway. Educational practice should prioritize reducing exclusion, strengthening belonging and social support, and providing accessible psychological support; general health-promoting strategies should remain complementary. Longitudinal, multimodal, and developmentally stratified studies are needed to test temporal ordering, mediation, and resilience.

records.title: Scientific research, governance, and sustainable development: Evidence from AI and digitalization research in the MENA region
records.authors: Ahmed El Oubani; Bouteina Elgharbaoui; Sara Chelh
records.abstract: Abstract The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for translating science and innovation into action rather than remaining at the theoretical level. However, evidence on whether scientific research translates into measurable sustainability outcomes remains limited, particularly for AI and digitalization research and in developing regions such as the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). This study examines whether scientific output in ‘AI and digitalization for sustainability’ is associated with improvements in the Sustainable Development Index (SDI) across 22 MENA countries. We employ a two-stage approach, a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in Scopus and Web of Science over the period 2010–2025, followed by a dynamic panel model estimated using difference GMM linking these publications to SDI. The bibliometric results reveal a rapidly expanding but unevenly distributed research landscape, concentrated in a few leading countries and organized around three complementary themes: predictive climate analytics, AI and digitalization applications tied to energy and sustainability, and the managerial frameworks guiding their implementation. Econometrically, publications are positively associated with SDI performance, with the effect emerging only after a three-year lag, consistent with a knowledge-diffusion process. Governance plays a decisive moderating role, substantially amplifying this effect in well-governed countries while it becomes negligible in weakly governed ones. The study provides new empirical evidence on how AI and digitalization research contributes to sustainability outcomes in a rapidly digitalizing yet climate-vulnerable developing region.

records.title: Investigating the Utilisation of Integrated Logistics System within the Ministry of Defence and Veteran Affairs in Khomas Region
records.authors: Dorothea Amwele; Helvi Ndilimeke Petrus
records.abstract: The effective utilisation of Integrated Logistics Systems (ILS) is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of operational efficiency, accountability, and readiness within defence organisations. The study investigated the utilisation of Integrated Logistics Systems within the Ministry of Defence and Veteran Affairs (MODVA) in the Khomas region of Namibia. A qualitative research approach was utilised, and data was gathered through semi-structured interviews with 33 participants drawn from logistics officers, supply chain managers, system administrators, and information technology support personnel. The data was analysed thematically to generate insights into patterns of system use, organisational dynamics, and user experiences. The findings revealed that although the Integrated Logistics System operates within MODVA, its use is still inconsistent, disjointed, and primarily confined to fundamental functions. Advanced system features intended to enhance complete logistics integration, real-time visibility, and strategic decision-making are greatly underused. The study also identified internal organisational elements such as leadership styles, corporate culture, workflow inconsistencies, inadequate training, and lack of ICT support as key factors influencing system utilisation. Participants also described national ICT infrastructure, procurement regulations, reliance on external suppliers, and cybersecurity requirements as contextual constraints affecting the environment in which ILS is used. Moreover, the study found that the challenges related to ILS implementation and utilisation are closely linked. Insufficient rollout planning, minimal user engagement, ineffective change management tactics, and ongoing training and capability deficiencies have led to diminished user trust and opposition to digital processes. Technical and infrastructural limitations further diminish trust in the system, while behavioural obstacles such as fear of making mistakes, preference for manual processes, and reluctance to change remain firmly embedded in the organisational culture. The study concludes that effective ILS implementation within MODVA necessitates a comprehensive strategy that combines technological proficiency with organisational preparedness, leadership commitment, ongoing skills enhancement, and organised change management. The findings contribute to the understanding of digital logistics systems adoption in defence settings in developing countries and offer evidence-based recommendations for improving system usage and operational efficiency.

records.title: Multidrug Resistance and Host Adaptation in Candida Auris: From Molecular Mechanisms to Emerging Therapeutic Frontiers
records.authors: Fenglin Shao; Tingru Wu; Jingjing Su
records.abstract: C. auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant (MDR) fungal pathogen that poses an urgent threat to global public health. It is characterized by rapid nosocomial transmission, persistent environmental survival, and extensive cross-resistance to conventional antifungal therapies. This comprehensive narrative review bridges the fundamental molecular mechanisms of intrinsic and acquired antifungal resistance with host adaptation strategies and emerging clinical interventions. C. auris resistance is driven by a highly sophisticated network of genetic mutations and metabolic reprogramming distributed across six geographically distinct clades (I-VI), including the newly identified Clade VI from the Indomalayan zone. Azole resistance primarily relies on clade-specific point mutations in the target gene ERG11, synergistically amplified by TAC1b-driven transcriptional upregulation of the CDR1 efflux pump. Echinocandin resistance is predominantly mediated by conformational reshaping across three distinct hotspot regions of the FKS1 gene, bolstered by Hsp90-mediated stress compensatory networks. For polyenes, while clinical resistance is frequently overestimated by commercial assays, true tolerance mechanisms involved the depletion of target ergosterol and profound non-sterol-dependent sphingolipid remodeling. Beyond genomic modifications, C. auris exhibits significant phenotypic plasticity, forming robust, polysaccharide-rich biofilms on indwelling medical devices that confer profound physical drug tolerance. Clinically, the fungus demonstrates a strong cutaneous tropism-predominantly colonizing the axilla and groin-which acts as the primary reservoir for hospital outbreaks. Furthermore, experimental models reveal that C. auris actively exploits host immune deficiencies, specifically subverting the IL-17A/neutrophil/S100A8 axis, to evade immune clearance and establish persistent colonization. To overcome these formidable MDR bottlenecks, therapeutic paradigms are rapidly evolving. The integration of next-generation antifungals such as the long-acting echinocandin rezafungin, fosmanogepix, and ibrexafungerp, synergistic combination therapies, quorum-sensing inhibitors such as farnesol, and experimental nanocarrier delivery systems could represent promising frontiers to effectively dismantle the complex defense networks of C. auris.

records.title: Comprehensive genetic diversity analysis of rice (Oryza sativa L.) genotypes for yield and cooking quality traits using multivariate approaches
records.authors: S S M Pavan; K G Vishal; Surekha; K B Ashish; M Prakriti; C Rita; K Geetanjali; R Anjan
records.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) holds global significance owing to its substantial genetic diversity and widespread consumer acceptance. Nevertheless, the crop encounters persistent threats from both biotic and abiotic stresses, necessitating the systematic utilisation of its available genetic diversity through selection-based breeding strategies. The present investigation was undertaken at the Postgraduate Research Farm of Centurion University of Technology and Management, Odisha, during the kharif season of 2025. Forty rice genotypes were evaluated in a randomised complete block design with 3 replications. Mahalanobis D² analysis grouped all forty genotypes into six clusters using Tocher’s method. The maximum inter-cluster distance between clusters III and IV identifying crosses between these groups as promising namely RNR 15435 × Pusa Basmati 1850 and Kalma × MTU 1081 for recovering potentially superior transgressive segregants. Seed protein content was found to be the highest contributor to total genetic divergence. Principal component analysis yielded eight significant components, explaining 79.16 % of cumulative variability. The PC1 and PC2 together accounted for 38.50 %, driven primarily by grain weight, breadth and kernel length traits. Biplot analysis identified Mawaii, Bhuraj, RGL 1880 and Kalorat as superior for grain shape and cooking quality and Judi dhan, RNR 15435 and Manipur local as promising for yield components indicating their potential for exploiting maximum genetic distance and developing improved rice varieties suited to Odisha.

records.title: HECO: A lightweight CMEMS-based oil-spill risk-assessment tool
records.authors: Gianfranco Di Pietro; Massimiliano Marino; Martina Stagnitti; Elisa Castro; Sofia Nasca; Luca Cavallaro; Enrico Foti; Rosaria Ester Musumeci
records.abstract: Oil spills pose significant threats to marine ecosystems and coastal economies; therefore, rapid and effective emergency response is critical. Although operational forecasting models can provide highly accurate simulations, they require domain specialists to make decisions about environmental vulnerabilities. This technical barrier creates an accessibility gap that can delay situational awareness during the first hours of an emergency, particularly for local authorities without dedicated expertise. HECO (Here Comes the Oil) is an open-source, Python-based Lagrangian particle dispersion model (LPDM) powered by the Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). The model was evaluated through a hindcast of the August 2021 Baniyas spill, using successive Sentinel-1 SAR-derived footprints for validation. The best-performing configuration covered 86.9% of the observed area with a Jaccard index of 61.7% and a Dice similarity coefficient of 76.3%, while completing the entire simulation and output-generation workflow in less than 15 min on a standard laptop. The model also demonstrates high robustness to variations in released oil volume and perturbations in spill origin. This shows the model’s significant geometric reliability for rapid hazard mapping during the early stages of an emergency response. HECO is intended for rapid, first-tier surface-hazard assessment by non-specialist users. By lowering the technical barriers to spatial hazard assessment, it enables first responders to rapidly quickly identify safe navigation zones and prioritize coastal protection strategies while awaiting more advanced operational modeling.

records.title: Multivariate analysis of poverty and social exclusion across EU countries in the context of Sustainable Development Goal 1
records.authors: Silvia Megyesiova; Cecilia Olexova
records.abstract: Poverty reduction remains one of the socio-economic concerns of the international agenda. This research aims to examine the multidimensional nature of poverty across EU Member States through a multivariate analysis of selected socio-economic indicators. Ten indicators were initially selected to capture the multidimensional nature of poverty and the broader socio-economic situation encompassing income poverty and deprivation within the sustainable development goal 1, housing conditions, economic performance and digital factors. Based on the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin test and subsequent statistical analyses, six indicators were retained for the final multivariate analysis. Data were drawn from the Eurostat Database. Univariate and multivariate statistical techniques were applied during the analyses. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to find linear relationships between pairs of indicators, while a principal component analysis and a cluster analysis were implemented to examine multidimensional structures and patterns. The multivariate analysis was conducted across three time spans: 2015–2019, 2020 (analysed separately as the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted economies) and 2021–2023. The results reveal a general decline in poverty; nevertheless, they also emphasise persistent regional disparities across EU Member States. Bulgaria, Greece, Romania, and Latvia form the most vulnerable cluster in the final period, whereas several countries in Northern and Western Europe show more stable trends. The results further indicate that multidimensional poverty profiles cannot be explained solely by economic performance or geographical location. In conclusion, the cluster-based approach provides a dynamic perspective on the diverse experiences of poverty in the EU. The results show the need for tailored policy responses that reflect the specificities of individual EU countries and clusters to promote sustainable and inclusive development and to strengthen resilience to potential future crises.

records.title: Prevalence and Patterns of War-Related Traumatic Event Exposure among Uganda People's Defense Forces (UPDF) Combatants: A Cross-Sectional Study
records.authors: Tumushabe Humbly; Herbert E. Ainemaani; Steven Nzamuhiki; Gerald Kiiza
records.abstract: Background: Military personnel deployed in counter-insurgency and regional peacekeeping operations face high frequencies of war-related traumatic stressors (Ibrahim, Akindele, & Useh, 2023). Within East Africa, the Uganda People’s Defense Forces (UPDF) have historically been engaged in intense combat theatres, including missions against the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), Al-Shabaab in Somalia under the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS), and allied regional stabilisation efforts (Bullman, T. A., et al., 2021). Despite mounting clinical evidence linking combat exposure to post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive disorder (MDD), and operational functional impairment, there remains a critical empirical gap regarding the exact cumulative burden and specific patterns of traumatic event exposure among active-duty UPDF combatants (Namatovu, S. et al., 2024). Statement of the Problem: Comprehensive epidemiological mapping of combat trauma patterns within African national militaries is notably sparse. Existing psychiatric literature predominantly relies on Western cohorts, whose operational doctrines, pre-enlistment socioeconomic stressors, and cultural idioms of distress diverge significantly from those of sub-Saharan African service members (Adebowale & Owoeye, 2021). Consequently, military medical planners lack localised empirical data to calibrate preventive mental health interventions, psych education, and trauma-informed psychological first aid within the UPDF barracks and forward operating bases (MacGregor, A. J., et al., 2023). Objectives: This cross-sectional study aims to quantify the prevalence and multidimensional patterns of war-related traumatic event exposure among active-duty UPDF combatants, examine the specific classes of operational stressors experienced, evaluate demographic and service-related risk factors, and determine the co-occurrence of trauma classes with clinical distress metrics. Literature Review: Decades of military psychological research, exemplified by landmark epidemiological studies within modern defence forces, demonstrate that cumulative trauma exposure operates in a dose-response relationship with psychopathology (Kamara & Bangura, 2023). Frameworks of continuous traumatic stress and combat-induced moral injury highlight factors such as witnessing friendly casualties, engaging in direct combat fire, handling human remains, and operating under asymmetric threat conditions exponentially elevate the risk of chronic psychological morbidity (Kigozi, F…, et al. 2022). Within African peacekeeping contexts, structural hardships, lack of post-deployment decompression, and combat intensity interact to magnify trauma vulnerability. Methodology: Utilising an analytical cross-sectional design, a stratified random sample of N=850 active-duty UPDF combatants was surveyed across multiple operational battalions and garrison commands. Data collection utilized standardized, culturally adapted instruments including the Traumatic Life Events Questionnaire (TLEQ), the Combat Exposure Scale (CES), and the Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Descriptive statistics, multivariate logistic regressions, and latent class analysis (LCA) were deployed to model trauma exposure profiles. Results: The overall prevalence of high-severity war-related traumatic event exposure was found to be "84.7% (n = 688)". Combatants reported an average of 6.2±2.4 distinct types of traumatic events. Latent class modelling isolated three distinct trauma exposure profiles: Low-Exposure Support Personnel, High Combat Direct-Engagement, and Asymmetric/Atrocity-Witnessed Trauma. Combat exposure scale scores were significantly elevated among infantry units deployed in external theatres compared to domestic administrative posts. Regression analyses indicated that direct exposure to improvised explosive devices (IEDs) and witnessing severe bodily mutilation or fatalities strongly predicted elevated PCL-5 scores. Conclusions: Active-duty UPDF combatants experience an immense, multidimensional burden of war-related traumatic stressors that heavily correlates with clinical symptom severity. Recommendations: The UPDF medical command should institutionalise mandatory post-deployment psychological screening, establish confidential, culturally resonant peer-support networks, and integrate specialised trauma-focused cognitive behavioural therapies (TF-CBT) within military health facilities.

records.title: Weather and health shocks in rural Uganda: heterogeneous consumption effects and coping strategies
records.authors: Emily Injete Amondo; Lukas Kornher; Rosemary Emegu Isoto; Alisher Mirzabaev; Bernard Bashaasha; Joachim von Braun
records.abstract: Abstract Background Compound and cascading shocks are common in rural areas and pose significant threats to food security and household welfare. While the importance of these combined shocks for rural communities is gaining attention, there is still very limited empirical research on the topic. This paper aims to assess the joint effects of weather and health shocks on the food, non-food, and total consumption of rural households in Uganda while also exploring heterogeneity in these effects across households and discussing the underlying mechanisms and coping strategies Our analysis uses customized high-frequency panel household survey data collected across six waves, employing fixed effects quantile regression method and a control function approach to address the potential endogeneity of health shocks. Results The findings indicate that a short-term increase in temperature above the long-term average is associated with a reduction in total and non-food consumption by approximately 15–26%. Among poorer households, the association between temperature and non-food consumption is particularly strong, exceeding 30%. Moreover, lagged temperature shocks are associated with significant declines in non-food consumption across all quantiles. This pattern suggests that the relationship between heat stress and household welfare may extend beyond the immediate exposure period. Higher lagged temperatures amplify the hospitalization–food consumption relationship. Positive rainfall deviations increases average food consumption overall but has heterogeneous effects across the distribution, reducing food consumption at the 20th–40th percentiles and increasing it at the 60th–80th percentiles, and compounds the adverse effect of prolonged illness. Additionally, the findings reveal considerable mobility in consumption among rural households over 12 months. Even households in the richest quartile may find themselves in the lowest consumption categories at certain times of the year. To manage these fluctuations in consumption, the poorest quartiles tend to rely on group networks and loans, while wealthier quartiles more frequently utilize remittances. Conclusion and policy implications Recognizing Uganda’s vulnerability to extreme weather events and epidemics, this paper suggests key policy measures. Enhancing social protection through access to credit, social networks, safety nets, and health insurance can help households cope with climate challenges. These strategies will strengthen food system resilience and promote sustainable development.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things in Smart Agriculture: A Bibliometric and Thematic Review of Data Infrastructures and Sustainability Implications
records.authors: ; ; ; Altyeb Ali Abaker Omer; Yajie Dong; ; ; Ibrahim Issa Mohamed Issa; ; Yousif Yahia Ahmed Abuker; ; Mohamed Ibrahim Abdallh Babeker; ; Alfadil Aboud Alfadil Hassan; ; Zhiguo Shan; ; Yinxue Shi;
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping smart agriculture through prediction, automation, resource optimization, and data-driven decision-making. However, its effective and sustainable deployment depends on reliable Internet of Things (IoT) data infrastructures supporting sensing, connectivity, data acquisition, transmission, and distributed processing. This review maps research at the intersection of AI, IoT, and smart agriculture and examines its data-infrastructure requirements and sustainability implications. Drawing on 441 Scopus-indexed, peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2017 and 2025, the study combines bibliometric performance analysis, science mapping, and content-based thematic interpretation to identify publication trends, intellectual foundations, influential research fronts, emerging themes, and deployment challenges. The bibliometric analyses characterize AI–IoT research in smart agriculture, while IoT data infrastructure provides the principal analytical lens, and sustainability and responsible deployment are examined through interpretive synthesis. The findings reveal rapid publication growth and prominent themes involving connected sensing, predictive analytics, edge intelligence, remote sensing, smart irrigation, cybersecurity, blockchain, and edge–cloud processing. Persistent barriers include limited interoperability, inconsistent data quality, energy requirements, scalability constraints, cybersecurity and governance risks, affordability, and unequal adoption in resource-constrained contexts. The review concludes that sustainable AI-enabled agriculture requires reliable, secure, interoperable, energy-efficient, inclusive, and context-appropriate digital infrastructures.

records.abstract: Climate change poses a serious threat to agricultural productivity, rural livelihoods and food security in Enugu State, Nigeria. Rising temperatures, irregular rainfall, flooding, soil degradation and erosion increase farmers’ vulnerability and may reduce crop yields. Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides emerging opportunities to address these challenges through data-driven and climate-smart agricultural practices. This paper examines the role of AI, climate-change adaptation and sustainable agriculture in improving food security in Enugu State. The study adopts a qualitative desk-review approach, drawing on relevant scholarly literature, policy documents and institutional reports. It examines AI applications in weather forecasting, crop and soil monitoring, pest and disease detection, precision farming, irrigation management, yield prediction and digital agricultural extension services. However, inadequate digital infrastructure, limited technical skills, high technology costs, poor internet connectivity, insufficient agricultural data and weak extension services may constrain adoption, particularly among smallholder farmers. The paper recommends investment in digital infrastructure, farmer training, affordable AI technologies, research, extension services and supportive policies to strengthen sustainable food production and food security in Enugu State.

records.title: Genuine risks or a threat to academic autonomy? Critical reflections on research ethics reviews of studies involving ‘vulnerable’ children and young people
records.authors: Chae-Young Kim; Martyn Hammersley
records.abstract: The ‘vulnerability’ of research participants is often a key issue in research ethics reviews. This paper critically reflects on the requirements laid down by Research Ethics Committees (RECs) to protect participants in research involving children and young people. It explores how particular assumptions about participant vulnerability may, in some cases, shape RECs’ decisions in ways that affect academic autonomy and potentially compromise the quality of research. To illustrate this, the paper examines two different UK university RECs’ reviews of two related studies involving secondary school students. In particular, it applies an approach informed by the casuistical ethical tradition to analyse the RECs’ decision letters and considers their impact on both studies. The analysis suggests that specific interpretations of vulnerability and risk, alongside a tendency to underestimate the competence and capacity for autonomy of young participants, contributed to constraints that adversely affected data collection and analysis in these studies. Given that the examples discussed are unlikely to be exceptional, the paper suggests that aspects of research ethics review processes warrant reconsideration to ensure that research involving children and young people can fulfil its objectives while upholding appropriate ethical standards.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in pharmacy practice in the Middle East: a scoping review of applications, adoption, barriers, and future directions
records.authors: Faten Alhomoud
records.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming pharmacy practice by supporting medication management, clinical decision-making, patient education, and pharmacy operations. Although AI research in the Middle East has expanded rapidly, the evidence remains fragmented across countries, technologies, and practice settings. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the current evidence on AI applications, adoption, perceived benefits, implementation barriers, and ethical and regulatory considerations in pharmacy practice across the Middle East. Methods A scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched for English-language studies investigating AI in pharmacy practice in Middle Eastern countries. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were synthesized narratively according to AI applications, utilization, pharmacists' awareness and attitudes, perceived benefits, implementation barriers, ethical and regulatory issues, and future research priorities. Results A total of 15 studies published between 2023 and 2026, involving 8,117 participants across multiple Middle Eastern countries, were included. Most studies were cross-sectional surveys (93.3%) evaluating pharmacists' awareness, perceptions, and readiness to adopt AI. ChatGPT and large language models were the most frequently investigated technologies, primarily supporting medication information, patient counselling, medication management, and clinical decision support, while AI-enabled robotics focused on dispensing and pharmacy operations. Pharmacists generally demonstrated high awareness and positive attitudes toward AI, and some studies reported previous or individual use; however, evidence of routine use and organization-level implementation remained limited. Perceived benefits included improved clinical decision-making, medication safety, and workflow efficiency, whereas major barriers included inadequate AI training, limited technological infrastructure, implementation costs, organizational readiness, and concerns regarding privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, and professional accountability. Conclusion AI has considerable potential to enhance pharmacy practice across the Middle East, but implementation remains at an early stage, with the available literature predominantly reflecting pharmacists' perceptions of anticipated benefits rather than evidence of demonstrated clinical effectiveness. Strengthening AI education, digital infrastructure, governance frameworks, and implementation research will be essential to support the safe, ethical, and evidence-based integration of AI into pharmacy practice.

records.title: Digital Transformation and the Future of the Accounting Profession: Accountants' Emerging Digital Technology Roles
records.authors: Odinakachukwu Ifeanyichukwu Ogaluzor
records.abstract: The accounting profession is experiencing unprecedented transformation due to rapid advancements in digital technologies and the increasing complexity of modern business environments. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data analytics, cloud computing, blockchain, robotic process automation, enterprise resource planning systems, and cybersecurity solutions are redefining the traditional functions of accountants and creating new opportunities for professional value creation. This paper examines the evolving roles, responsibilities, and competencies of accountants in a technology-driven world and explores the implications of these developments for accounting education and professional practice in Nigeria. Adopting a narrative literature review and conceptual analysis approach, the study synthesizes evidence from scholarly literature, professional accounting reports, policy documents, and contemporary empirical studies. The review reveals that accountants are increasingly functioning as strategic business partners, data analysts, governance champions, risk management specialists, technology integrators, forensic accounting experts, tax advisors, sustainability reporting professionals, financial consultants, and cybersecurity collaborators. The study further finds that while technology has automated many routine accounting tasks, it has simultaneously increased the demand for higher-order competencies such as analytical thinking, digital literacy, professional judgment, strategic decision-making, communication, and ethical reasoning. The paper concludes that the future relevance of accountants depends largely on their ability to adapt to technological change through continuous learning and competency development. The study recommends curriculum reforms, enhanced professional training, stronger industry-academia collaboration, regulatory support, and sustained investments in digital capacity development to ensure that accountants remain relevant and effective in the evolving digital economy.

records.title: Biodigital Transformation and Multidisciplinary Treatment Planning in Dentistry
records.authors: Gizem Yazdan Özen
records.abstract: Digitalization in dentistry signifies a new era that goes beyond transferring imaging, impression-taking, design, and manufacturing stages to computer-aided systems and requires biological characteristics, clinical findings, patient preferences, and long-term risks to be evaluated within a shared data model. In this chapter, “biodigital dentistry” is defined as the integration of patients’ clinical, radiological, morphological, functional, and, when necessary, molecular data through digital technologies and the use of this integrated information in diagnosis, treatment simulation, interdisciplinary sequencing, manufacturing, and monitoring processes. The historical development of the transition from conventional to digital workflows, virtual patient creation, clinical–radiological–digital data fusion, artificial intelligence-assisted decision-support systems, the timing of periodontal–orthodontic–surgical–restorative treatments, and personalized care models are discussed in light of current evidence. Ethical and legal issues, including algorithmic bias, explainability, data minimization, cybersecurity, informed consent, and the domestic and international transfer of health data, are also evaluated in terms of clinical applicability. The principal objective of the biodigital transformation is not to replace the clinician but to facilitate more predictable decision-making for the right patient, at the right time, and within biological limits. Successful implementation requires an interoperable data infrastructure, validated technologies, shared interdisciplinary objectives, human oversight, and continuous outcome monitoring.

records.title: What “Digitization” Means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port (Cameroon) Project: Definitions, Components, Pathways, and Implications
records.authors: alfred ndi
records.abstract: Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port in Cameroon by situating the concept within port operational processes, stakeholder relationships, governance environments, and socioeconomic constraints specific to Limbe and comparable West/Central African ports. Drawing on an interdisciplinary desk-based literature review of academic studies, international agency reports, industry white papers, and regional policy documents, the study adopts a conceptual-analytical approach to define digitization as the systematic conversion and integration of analogue and paper-based port procedures into interoperable digital systems that enable real-time data exchange, automated workflows, evidence-based decision-making, and secure electronic transactions across the port ecosystem. The paper disaggregates digitization into technological (TOS, PCS, VTMS, IoT, analytics, blockchain, cybersecurity), organizational (process re-engineering, governance, procurement), human factors (skills, roles, change management), and regulatory (single window, data governance) dimensions. It identifies measurable indicators to assess progress—transaction digitalization rate, vessel turnaround time, dwell time, customs clearance time, system uptime, and workforce certification rates—and outlines likely benefits (efficiency, transparency, environmental monitoring, regional connectivity) and risks (digital divides, cyber threats, governance bottlenecks, finance constraints). The analysis highlights contextual enablers and barriers for Limbe, including infrastructure, institutional capacity, financing options, and regional integration imperatives. The paper concludes with policy and operational recommendations that prioritize staged interventions—low‑complexity quick wins, mid‑term integration, and long‑term smart-port capabilities—anchored in inclusive governance, blended finance, workforce development, and cyber resilience. The findings aim to provide a clear, practical, and academically grounded definition of digitization tailored to Limbe’s developmental and geopolitical realities. Keywords: Limbe Deep Sea Port; port digitization; Port Community System; Terminal Operating System; Cameroon; smart ports; maritime governance

records.title: Challenges of Financial Inclusion in Himachal Pradesh: A Comprehensive Analysis of Barriers and Progress
records.authors: Farooq Akmal; Munish Dulta
records.abstract: The study includes an analysis of the achievements and key constraints in financial inclusion in HP, including financial outreach, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), and digital financial services, credit, insurance, and limiting factors in the usage of formal financial services. The study aims at two major objectives: one, to look at the status of financial inclusion in HP, and two, to outline the major challenges for financial inclusion in HP. The research design uses descriptive and analytical research, with the primary source of data from secondary sources. The information is extracted from RBI, NABARD Reports, PMJDY statistics, Government reports, national surveys, and peer-reviewed empirical studies with peer reviews. Progress and barriers to progress are measured through tabular analysis, trend examination, and thematic synthesis. The results indicate significant strides in financial inclusion, including a robust network of banks and financial institutions in the rural areas, increasing bank deposits and advances, and an estimated 20.17 lakh PMJDY accounts by August 2026. But inclusion is still hampered by the ruggedness of the terrain, the lack of digital infrastructure, financial and digital illiteracy, access–usage gap, credit exclusion, low insurance coverage, cybersecurity and trust issues. The study is a contribution to the literature as the financial inclusion in the state of HP has been assessed in an integrated and multidimensional manner, which involves the banking infrastructure, government programmes, digital finance, credit, insurance, and unique geographical issues facing the state. The study recommends that policy should shift from mere ownership to accessible, affordable, secure, and widely adopted financial services, supported by a more robust digital system, financial literacy, locally relevant banking distribution channels, inclusive credit, and adequate micro-insurance.

records.title: Viral threats to maize: understanding host-virus interactions and sustainable management
records.authors: Muhammad Junaid; Jinhao Xie; Hao Wang; Muhammad Dilshad Hussain; Laihua Dong; Dezhi Peng; Zhengxing Song; Liyang Xie; Qin Yan; Pei Wang; Junxia Hu; Euclides de Sousa Vilanova; João Roberto Spotti Lopes; Yan Zhang; Fei Jiang; Kaitong Du; Tao Zhou
records.abstract: Abstract Viral diseases represent one of the most serious constraints to global maize production, where increasing disease incidence and expanding viral diversity threaten yield stability and food security. Several viruses are recognized as the most economically important pathogens in maize. Maize-infecting viruses employ sophisticated infection strategies that suppress host immunity, manipulate hormonal and redox signaling, and exploit insect vectors to drive rapid and widespread transmission. Synergistic interactions among some co-infecting viruses further intensify disease severity, frequently leading to devastating epidemics. In this review, we highlight the top 10 economically significant maize viruses and summarize key profiles for each. We highlight recent advances in understanding how maize viruses modulate host defenses through RNA-silencing suppressors and regulatory networks involving microRNAs (miRNAs) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. We also discuss progress in diagnostics and genetic tools, including portable detection platforms, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based assays, and virus-derived vectors, which are enhancing disease surveillance. Finally, we summarize current control strategies, with an emphasis on RNA interference (RNAi)-based and biotechnology-mediated resistance, and outline critical research gaps concerning resistance mechanisms, vector biology, and viral synergism.

records.title: Gender Justice Activism and Strategic Abeyance in Post-2020 Hong Kong
records.authors: Mengzhe Feng
records.abstract: This article examines the post-2020 transformation of Hong Kong’s gender justice movement amid autocratization. Drawing on 20 in-depth interviews and public materials, it develops a profile-shaped framework of abeyance to demonstrate that political risks and adaptive possibilities are distributed unevenly across civil society. The study argues that, as a lower-profile sector, gender justice activism faces less direct repression, retains institutional space unavailable to higher-profile pro-democracy movement, and absorbs redirected civic energy. It then demonstrates how activists adapt through self-limitation, arena shifts, and reorganizing structures to exploit this tolerable position. This delicate navigation allows them to remain active without being reclassified as threats in the eyes of authorities. The findings offer broader insights into authoritarian governance, contemporary civil society survival, and movement adaptation in non-democratic contexts.

records.title: When climate risk intensifies, does insurance pay off? A community case study of China's agricultural insurance reform
records.authors: Changzhe Deng; Maimiao Sun; Xueyu Lin; Chencan Rao; Qiuping Guo
records.abstract: In the context of mounting global climate threats, fostering resilience in food production systems has become a critical imperative for upholding national food security. This paper exploits the staggered implementation, beginning in 2018, of China's agricultural insurance reforms covering full production costs and planting income as a quasi-natural experiment. Drawing on provincial panel data from 2013 to 2024, we first develop a multidimensional composite index to capture food production resilience. A staggered difference-in-differences specification is then adopted to systematically assess the causal effect of these reforms on such resilience and to explore the underlying transmission channels. Moreover, from a novel climate change perspective, the analysis examines the heterogeneous treatment effects across varying degrees of climate risk exposure. The empirical findings reveal that the policy-led agricultural insurance reform significantly and robustly enhances China's food production resilience. Mechanism tests indicate that advances in agricultural technology and the expansion of large-scale farming operations serve as important pathways through which the insurance policy takes effect. Further investigation shows that climate change risk positively moderates the policy impact: as climate risk intensifies, the marginal contribution of insurance to resilience becomes stronger. Heterogeneity analysis also demonstrates that the policy effect is more pronounced in western China and in localities with higher rates of disaster-induced losses. Taken together, these results offer solid empirical backing for broadening the pilot programs of full cost and planting income insurance. They also establish a theoretical basis for positioning publicly supported agricultural insurance as an effective instrument for climate change adaptation, providing valuable guidance on strengthening the climate adaptability and resilience of food production to ensure national food security.

records.title: The ReDiKid framework: a transdisciplinary systems approach to child resilience in the digital age
records.authors: Jana Pelclová; Leen d’Haenens; Marc N. Potenza; Jaroslava Suchá; Aleš Gába; Tomas Vetrovsky; David Šmahel; Roman Procházka; Adeela ahmed Shafi
records.abstract: Children’s lives are increasingly shaped by digital environments that influence learning, social relationships, daily routines, and exposure to both opportunities and adversity. However, existing approaches often examine digital experiences, self-regulation, movement behaviors, and social context separately. This paper introduces ReDiKid (Resilient Kid in the Digital World), a developmental-systems framework for understanding resilience in late childhood, with a primary focus on children aged approximately 9–11 years. ReDiKid conceptualizes resilience as a higher-order, adversity-activated process through which adaptive functioning is maintained, restored, or reorganized over time. The framework integrates four interacting domains: psychophysiological, behavioral, contextual, and digital. It proposes four cross-domain pathways, self-regulatory capacity, movement regulation, social buffering, and digital competence, through which resources and vulnerabilities may shape responses to adversity, recovery, and subsequent adaptation. The framework distinguishes digital adversity from normative digital demands and differentiates resilience from competence, adaptive functioning, and multidimensional wellbeing. Six directional and empirically contestable propositions specify expected within-person, between-person, event-level, and contextual patterns, including conditions under which the propositions would not be supported. ReDiKid also recognizes that pathway operation may vary according to developmental stage, sex and gender, structural inequality, cultural context, neurodivergence, disability, and patterns of digital access. To support empirical testing, ReDiKid outlines a multimodal methodological architecture combining intensive longitudinal designs, ecological momentary assessment, wearable sensing, passive digital tracking, contextual data, and advanced longitudinal and multilevel analyses. ReDiKid provides a common conceptual foundation for coordinated study-specific protocols and cumulative theory development concerning child resilience in digitally mediated contexts.

records.title: Prevalence, risk factors, and pain trajectories for persistent pain after repeated cesarean delivery: a prospective observational study
records.authors: Caijuan Li; Minhui Wu; Mao Mao; Fan Xia; Shanwu Feng; Zhiqiang Zhou
records.abstract: Abstract Background Persistent maternal pain following cesarean delivery (CD) is common and can have deleterious consequences. Data about persistent pain characteristics, including distribution, predictors and trajectories following CD, especially in women undergoing repeated CD, are still limited. Methods This prospective observational study was performed at the Women’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from May 2022 to November 2023 to identify factors associated with persistent pain in this cohort by LASSO and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Pain scores and anatomical locations were recorded through 90 days post‑CD to delineate temporal patterns. And we also performed an exploratory analysis of postoperative pain trajectory distributions among the parturient by LCMM analysis. Results Of the 360 parturient women enrolled, 357 completed the final analysis of prevalence, risk factors, and pain trajectory. Pain prevalence after repeated CD fell sharply over time, from 99.7% on postoperative day (POD) 1 to 25.9% by POD 90. Multivariable logistic regression identified two independent risk factors for persistent pain at POD 90 using LASSO-selected variables across 20 imputed datasets: anxiety (adjusted OR 2.933; 95% CI 1.55 to 5.549; P = 0.001) and higher uterine contraction pain score on POD 1 (adjusted OR 1.174; 95% CI 1.015 to 1.361; P = 0.031). The logistic model showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.638; 95% CI 0.571 to 0.706). At the optimal cutoff of 0.259, sensitivity was 50.0% and specificity was 74.0%. An exploratory LCMM analysis identified three 90-day pain trajectories after repeated CD: Slow recovery from severe pain (Class 1, 37 (10.4%)), Persistent moderate pain (Class 2, 30 (8.4%)), and Consistent low pain (Class 3, 290 (81.2%)). Conclusions Approximately one in four women experience all-caused postoperative pain at day 90 following repeated CD. Prenatal anxiety and greater visceral pain at POD 1 are associated with higher likelihood of reporting persistent pain, with only modest discriminatory power. Further multi-center studies are needed to explore better interventions, such as emotional reassurance or multimodal analgesia, in anxious parturient when undergoing repeated CD. Exploratory trajectory analysis indicates a subset at higher risk either follow a slow-recovery trajectory or remain in a persistent pain state, who will also require increased attention in the future. Trial registration This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2200059487) on 02/05/2022.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Smart Grid and Renewable Energy Management: A Review of Techniques, Applications, and Future Directions
records.authors: Udit Vaibhav Pant, Om Zile; Sahil Kumar Singh, Anurag Banerjee
records.abstract: Intermittent renewable generation, volatile loads, and concerns over grid stability have become defining features of modern power systems. Addressing these challenges with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is attracting growing attention, including through better forecasting, automated demand response, optimized energy storage, and smart grid fault detection. This paper highlights the various AI-based techniques developed across the smart grid landscape, ranging from solar and wind forecasting to short-term load forecasting, demand-side management, electricity price forecasting, energy storage and battery management, grid resilience, and digital twins. It offers an overview of recently published work, including the major approaches, namely deep learning (LSTM and Transformer models), explainable AI, multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, and federated learning, together with their strengths and limitations. The paper also presents a conceptual three-layer framework comprising edge sensing, federated forecasting and control, and explainable operator support at the distribution-utility level; the framework is not validated empirically. Challenges such as data privacy, model interpretability, scalability, and cybersecurity are explored, together with future research directions and the relevance of these technologies to India’s energy transition goals.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and digital technologies in railway systems: a systematic literature review using the TCCM framework
records.authors: Mukesh Kumar Meena; Gautam Kumar; Rajendra Kumar Meena
records.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries worldwide, driving digital innovation operational efficiency, safety, reliability and overall sustainability. Additionally, associated technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins and the Internet of Things (IoT) have further accelerated the digital transformation across railway systems. The literature in this domain is still at a developmental stage and remains fragmented across multiple application domains. This limits the understanding of theoretical foundations, context and methodological approaches. Design/methodology/approach To address this gap, this study conducts a hybrid systematic literature review using thematic analysis of bibliometric data from 121 Scopus records followed by application of the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework on a subset of the literature identified through systematic screening based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Findings The theoretical and conceptual development in this domain is strongly focused on the themes relating to predictive maintenance, infrastructure monitoring and operational optimisation. Novel technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins and the IoT emerge as the most frequently discussed technologies in the context of adoption within existing systems. The integrated TCCM analysis identifies three broad trajectories: a technology-integration trajectory centred on digital twins, cyber-physical systems and Industry 4.0/5.0; an algorithmic trajectory centred on AI, machine learning, deep learning and prognostics; and a decision-optimisation trajectory involving multi-criteria decision-making, fuzzy logic and intelligent transport systems. There is a comparatively higher concentration of literature on developed economies. Freight and logistics, despite emerging as an important thematic area, remain theoretically and methodologically fragmented, while emerging economies and several passenger- and sustainability-oriented applications receive limited attention. Methodologically, the literature is dominated by reviews, conceptual frameworks, modelling, simulation and experimental studies, with limited longitudinal evidence on the organisational and strategic consequences of AI adoption. There remains scope for stronger theoretical grounding, focusing on freight logistics, emerging technologies and longitudinal investigations to advance the literature. Originality/value This study provides a structured synthesis of the fragmented literature on AI and digital technologies in railway systems through the TCCM framework. It identifies key research gaps and proposes a future research agenda emphasising stronger theoretical foundations, freight-oriented applications, emerging technologies and longitudinal empirical investigations to support the development of intelligent and sustainable railway ecosystems.

records.title: Introducing PegasusAI Studio: A new way of Artificial Intelligence Assisted Workflow Management on National Cyberinfrastructure
records.authors: Rynge, Mats; Thareja, Komal; Vahi, Karan
records.abstract:
Workflows are a key technology for enabling complex scientific computations. They capture the interdependencies between processing steps in data analysis and simulation pipelines as well as the mechanisms to execute those steps reliably and efficiently. Workflows can capture complex processes, promote sharing and reuse, and also provide provenance information necessary for the verification of scientific results and scientific reproducibility. 

PegasusAI (https://pegasus-ai.org/) is an open, AI-infused workflow management framework that extends the Pegasus Workflow Management System to enable intelligent orchestration of scientific workflows across the computing continuum, spanning edge resources, cloud platforms, and high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The project integrates machine learning into workflow planning, resource provisioning, execution monitoring, anomaly detection, performance prediction, and adaptive workflow management, while providing role-based, human-in-the-loop interfaces for scientists, cyberinfrastructure facilitators, and CI operators. PegasusAI also produces curated, AI-ready workflow execution datasets and reusable models to accelerate research in AI for scientific workflows and cyberinfrastructure operations. By combining trusted workflow technologies with AI-driven decision support, PegasusAI aims to improve the resilience, efficiency, and accessibility of distributed scientific computing. 

As part of PegasusAI we have been working on a hosted deployment called PegasusAI Studio (studio.pegasus-ai.org), that allows users to build, run, monitor, and debug Pegasus workflows  with AI assistance — in one persistent browser workspace, from scientific intent to a running, inspectable run. PegasusAI Studio also comes with an in-built marketplace that features a variety of representative workflows from different science domains that users can use as a starting reference point for their workflows. Users can also generate workflows from the chat interface by combining their own prompts with workflow-specific skills, sent to whichever LLM backend they have connected.  PegasusAI studio leverages core pegasus monitoring and debugging tools augmented with AI capabilities, including new web-based monitoring tools that give real time feedback to the users about their running workflows. For workflow execution, the studio seamlessly also connects with a variety of national Cyber Infrastructure resources such as ACCESS, PATh Facility, the OSPool, Fabric and Chameleon. 

PegasusAI studio is under active development with its public release scheduled for November 2026. In this poster, we present the vision and architecture of PegasusAI Studio and give a preview of its capabilities. Pegasus AI is a joint collaboration between Information Sciences Institute (ISI) at University of Southern California, Renaissance Computing Institute (RENCI) at University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill, University of Tennessee at Knoxville and University of Massachusetts, Amherst.

records.title: Digital Health Ecosystems and Community Wellness: A Socio Technological Framework for Public Health Innovation
records.authors: Bindu Madhavi Mangalampalli; Sreoshi Dasgupta; K. ARPITHA; Gowhar Rashid Bhat; Piyal Roy; Saptarshi Kumar Sarkar
records.abstract: Digital health ecosystems are transforming the nature of healthcare delivery by integrating innovative technology, healthcare stakeholders and community resources to drive community health and population wellness. The present study examines the idea of digital health ecosystems to aid socio-technological systems of innovation in the domain of population health. The interpretivist philosophy, deductive approach, descriptive research design and secondary data collection methodology are embraced and applied in the study. To investigate the interplay of technological infrastructure, stakeholder engagement, governance mechanisms, and healthcare results, academic journals, healthcare reports, policy documents, and publications by international health organizations were used to gather data. The results indicate that digital health technologies, telemedicine, electronic health records, mobile health applications, wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing, have the potential to significantly enhance healthcare access, efficacy, and communication with patients. The analysis also shows that the stakeholder collaboration between the healthcare providers, policy formulators, technology innovators and communities results in an enhanced health awareness, disease prevention, management of chronic diseases and the quality of life in general. However, the challenges of digital inequalities, cyber threats, privacy, lack of proper infrastructure, and digital illiteracy also exist as issues to the effective implementation. The paper provides a socio-technological model integrating technological innovation, social and organizational variables to enhance sustainable healthcare change. Under the framework, the most significant elements in promoting the best benefit of community health are governance, community-related participation, and responsible digital health. Overall, the research concludes that the digital health ecosystems represent a promising path to creating more accessible, resilient, and patient-centered healthcare systems and improving long term community health and innovation in population health.

records.title: Integrating traditional ecological knowledge with ecological surveys for conservation of the Mishmi Takin in Eastern Himalaya, India
records.authors: Pariyal Jagannath Gaurav; Sirumai Khusiali Kri; Govindan Veeraswami Gopi
records.abstract: Integrating indigenous and scientific knowledge systems is increasingly recognised as essential tool for addressing conservation challenges in data-deficient landscapes. However, approaches for systematically incorporating Traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) into conservation science remain limited. In this study we evaluated weather TEK can function as structured ecological information for understanding the vulnerable Mishmi Takin ( Budorcas taxicolor taxicolor ) in the Eastern Himalayas. Between 2021 and 2023 TEK were documented from indigenous communities in Arunachal Pradesh, India. Community-derived ecological observations were integrated with camera trapping, field expeditions and direct observations. Multivariate analyses, including Principal Component Analyses (PCA), Multiple Correspondence Analyses (MCA), hierarchical clustering and regression approaches were used to examine patterns and variation in ecological knowledge. Respondents described seasonal migration, habitat use, congregation dynamics, group size, and perceived threats. Camera trap surveys (>17,000 independent captures) validated key observations, the habitat use patterns, identified critical congregation sites and seasonal aggregations. Multivariate analyses showed distinct gradients of ecological knowledge associated with landscape exposure, observation effort, and threat awareness demonstrating that TEK represents a structured knowledge system and can generate robust ecological information for data-deficient species. Our findings further underscored that the TEK can provide a reliable ecological inference and provide a robust source of evidence for understanding species ecology, identifying critical habitats and conservation. By integrating TEK with species ecology this study presents a replicable framework for conservation research and decision making in remote socio-ecological landscapes.

records.title: Intelligent Telemedicine Systems: Machine Learning for Remote Diagnosis and Patient Management
records.authors: Kasthuri Subaramaniam; Oras Baker; Asiah Lokman
records.abstract: Telemedicine has experienced significant evolution in the past 10 years from a communication-driven health service to an intelligent, data-driven environment driven by AI (artificial intelligence), ML (machine learning), IoMT (Internet of Medical Things) and cloud–edge computing. This development has been further advanced through ongoing global health challenges that have seen an ageing population, rising burden of chronic, multi-morbid conditions, healthcare specialist shortage, soaring cost of healthcare and major disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic. Modern telehealth services are now integrating more machine learning algorithms for remote diagnosis, real-time monitoring the patient, predictive risk stratification and proactive treatment. This paper offers a comprehensive academic overview of intelligent telemedicine systems using machine learning for remote diagnosis and patient management. It synthesises and reviews recent literature on image-based diagnostics, physiological time-series modelling, NLP algorithms used to interpret symptoms, and multimodal data fusion models. An integrated system architecture is proposed and presented to illustrate how IoMT devices, data collection pipelines, preprocessing layers, machine learning inbound engines, and clinician decision tools are interlinked in the digital telemedicine landscape. We evaluated a proof-of-concept machine learning workflow for short-term patient deterioration prediction, relying on synthetic IoMT-style patient datasets to demonstrate real-world feasibility and clinical relevance. Apart from technical performance, the paper also describes the challenges of data quality, interoperability, algorithmic bias, explainability, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and integration into clinical workflows. Ethical questions, including trust in intelligent healthcare, responsibility, patients’ autonomy, and fair treatment, are raised. Finally, opportunities for future research are mentioned, including digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI, autonomous IoMT ecosystems, and emotionally intelligent telemedicine platforms to guide researchers, clinicians, systems designers, and policy makers on the evolution of telemedicine in a way that is intelligent, proactive and just in health care.

records.title: Review research progress, critical reflections and future prospects of digital care for chronic diseases
records.authors: Yingchao Zhou; Ruizhe Cao; Yanwei Su
records.abstract: The global prevalence of chronic diseases is becoming increasingly severe, and traditional care models are confronted with multiple challenges, including uneven distribution of medical resources, insufficient continuity of care, and inadequate patient self-management capacity. The rapid iteration of digital technologies and the catalyst of the COVID-19 pandemic have driven chronic disease care into a new phase of digital transformation. Based on relevant studies published from 2021 to 2026, this paper structures its analysis around a core logical framework: evidence-based evidence, care models, population adaptability and practical implementation. It systematically reviews the core technical systems and innovative characteristics of care models in digital chronic disease care, deeply analyzes the adaptive differences across diverse populations and disease types, and conducts critical reflections from the perspectives of evidence quality, health equity, clinical applicability, and homogeneity in intervention design. Finally, it puts forward future development directions centered on precision, localization, equity, and integration. The study reveals that digital chronic disease care has formed four core technological systems in application: intelligent sensing, digital behavioral intervention, immersive technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) and big data. Care models demonstrate innovative trends of nurse leadership, multi-dimensional collaboration, and caregiver empowerment. Nevertheless, prominent issues persist, such as insufficient high-quality evidence, a striking digital divide, difficulties in clinical integration, and a lack of personalized design. In the future, deep integration of technological innovation with clinical demands, enhanced targeted interventions for vulnerable populations, implementation of localized long-term studies, and improvement of policy and ethical guarantee systems are required. These efforts will promote the shift of digital chronic disease care from technology-driven to evidence-driven and demand-driven models, ultimately improving the overall efficiency of chronic disease management and health equity.

records.title: A Comprehensive Study of Logistics 5.0 Adaptation & Challenges in the Indian Supply Chain Industry
records.authors: Pritha Chaturvedi; Soumyajyoti Bhattacharjee
records.abstract: Logistics 5.0 indicates the combination of Industry 5.0’s important principles such as human-centricity, resiliency, and sustainability with the advanced digital capabilities of Logistics 4.0. While a growing number of developed countries are starting to adopt AI, digital twins, collaborative robots, and human-machine decision-making systems, there is still only limited evidence available regarding Logistics 5.0 implementation in India. The purpose of this study is to find out the main technological, financial, human, infrastructural, regulatory, organizational, cultural, and sustainability hurdles on the way to Logistics 5.0 implementation in Indian logistics. We used a qualitative analysis of secondary data to conduct the research, using logistics cost assessments data, e-commerce and last mile markets data, previously conducted published studies in the field of Industry 4.0/5.0, and some examples from Delhivery Ltd. The results indicate that following improvements in the logistical cost efficiency of India and rapid growth in the e-commerce logistics, the utilization of technology is still inconsistent within the industry. Factors affecting its implementation include high costs of implementation, shortage of skilled workers, cybersecurity threats, poor lastmile infrastructure, lack of digital capabilities, and resistance within organizations to cooperate with machines. EXPERTS NOTE that most of the large firms in private and public sectors have made significant strides in implementing Logistics 5.0 while small and medium sized enterprises face numerous obstacles. The above article discusses readiness issues of the sector and proposes readiness roadmaps as well as specific steps in accordance with the National Logistics Policy of India and PM GatiShakti framework.

records.title: Autonomous Robotic Systems in Agriculture 5.0: A Review on Technical Architecture, Operational Applications, and Future Perspectives
records.authors: Mehmet Metin Özgüven
records.abstract: This comprehensive narrative review examines the current state and future development perspectives of autonomous robotic systems within the scope of the Agriculture 5.0 paradigm, which aims for sustainable and efficient agricultural production. Within the scope of field applications, the SAM2-based SPAF framework, which offers 95.54% harvesting success rate in tomatoes, and spot-spraying technologies that reduce chemical input volume by 90% are evaluated using quantitative data. Furthermore, the synergy between heterogeneous UAV-UGV fleets, trust-building through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and emerging advanced technological approaches such as Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) are assessed. The results demonstrate that autonomous agriculture is not merely a tool to enhance technical efficiency, but is transforming into a cyber-physical production ecosystem where ethical responsibility, data sovereignty, and environmental sustainability converge.
